institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore a destination that were different from studying in Copenhagen. Due to COVID-19 the choices were a bit limited, and therefore I ended up choosing Tromsø. At the same time studying in Tromsø opened up opportunities about choosing courses that included parts of the arctic culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy as almost all information was send to my KU-mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Fast replies on mail, when I had any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I had some troubles choosing the courses I wanted as I was nominated to the faculty of social sciences and economics courses was a part of the business school. However, I ended up getting aloid to take one economics course and two political science courses.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Not so easy. I wrote to a lot of people on
Finn.no
and
Hybel.no
, who rented out hybels/rooms, but most people preferred long-time renters. Luckily, I got contacted from a girl who was going on exchange herself, so I could rent her room while she was gone.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Tromsø there is no possibilities to live on-campus. A tip is to sign up for student housing as soon as possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found housing on my own, but I was really satisfied with my housing. I rented a room in a 'real' norwegian treehouse, which I shared with four norwegians.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As stated above, I was not aloid to take economic courses in the beginning (even though I'm an economic student) as I was nominated to the faculty of social sciences.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The first registration is based on your pre-approvals, where both your own university and the host university have to accept the chosen courses. If you want to change the courses in your pre-approval, you have to get approval from the responsible professor of the new course, and afterwards get approval from your own university+host university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much help from the host university as they kept saying that I was only aloided to take courses from the faculty I was nominated to.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end, I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be stubborn. Try to change to your preferred courses, even though they start saying that it is not possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course 'Models for Market Analysis' was very useful.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level in the economic course was the same as in Copenhagen. I think the level in the political science courses were a bit lower than I'm used to but pensum included more required reading that I'm used to. However, this is the first time for me taking political science courses, so it is a bit difficult to compare to the level in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Same kind of teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Models for Market Analysis
Global Political Economy
Northern Governance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Models for Market Analysis was on a high level and as I haven't been working in R studio before, the course was a good introduction to the tool.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Restaurants/bars were more expensive than expected even though I knew that food/alcohol prices were higher in Norway than in Denmark.
The public transportation opportunities were limited, and therefore you had to rent a car yourself, if you wanted to visit other places. I.e. even though public transportation was 'cheap', the cost of transportation including rent of cars was higher than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to COVID-19 the non-academic opportunities were limited.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
An organisation called 'ESN Tromsø, arranged social events for exchange students including hikes, mini-golf, smaller trips etc.
TSI is the local sport club for students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore the city and surroundings by hiking, sailing, driving etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Exploit the many outdoor activities: 
- hikes when the weather allows you
- weekend trips to Lofoten, Senja, Finland, Svalbard etc. 
- Skiing in the winter
- Chasing the northern light
- Whale safari
- Dog sledding
The number of outdoor activities is almost unlimited.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy as the norwegian culture is similar to the danish culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to live with locals, talk to your class mates, socialize in the climbing hall.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, but adapting to the artic climate was a bit difficult

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The positive-minded attitude toward the nature/climate even though the weather was bad.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open-minded and try new activities/food 
Join the ESN-events to become familiar with other exchange students
Take courses that include a local/arctic element

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't go to Tromsø if you don't like winter

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting to the arctic climate including lower temperature and polar nights

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
